The core insight is that GSE's evolution hinges on three interlocking primitives: event taxonomy (PostHog), autonomous execution (Trigger.dev), and AI traceability (Langfuse). These form a triadic structure where E(T) informs J(R,D), which in turn evaluates A(M,C). The failure mode occurs when any component lacks robustness—e.g., E(T) becomes noisy, J(R,D) fails to scale, or A(M,C) loses fidelity. Each primitive must be modularly integrated yet independently verifiable. The dualities lie in the symmetry between measurement (E) and action (J), and between observability (A) and control (J). This architecture supports retroactive learning through feedback loops, ensuring GSE evolves toward optimal performance states.
